title: Cause-specific Cox regression under competing risks
summary: The hazard ratio for one cause among people still event-free, with competing events censored for that model only.

sizing._why: The log-rank form counts all events; under competing risks the events of the cause of interest are fewer and depend on the competing rate. Sizing needs both hazards and is a simulation.

pinned_defaults: Both: the event is the cause of interest only (status == 1). Counting competing deaths as events (a composite) gives a log hazard ratio of -0.24 here against the cause-specific -0.38.
R: ties = 'efron' named; lifelines' CoxPHFitter uses Efron.
_rate_not_risk: A cause-specific hazard ratio compares RATES among those still event-free. It does not say how many people experience the event by a time point, which also depends on how fast the competing event removes people. Report the cumulative incidence (competing-risks-cumulative-incidence) beside it, and use a Fine-Gray model when the question is the effect on that cumulative incidence.
